title: Teriyaki salmon side
skill: Skinning and portioning a side of salmon

notes.text: For more than 6, buy a second side and roast the portions on two sheet pans, swapping them halfway.

move.title: A whole side, portioned
move.body: Fish counters charge more for portions than for a whole side. You'll pin-bone a side of salmon, take off the skin in one piece, cut it into even portions by weight, and roast them under a homemade teriyaki glaze reduced in a saucepan.

why.title: Pin bones first
why.body: Pin bones run in a line through the thick front half of the side. With the skin still on, the flesh holds firm while you pull each one out with tweezers, toward the head end.

why.title: Skin it in one pass
why.body: Start at the tail end. Cut down to the skin, angle the blade flat against it, and grip the skin tail with a paper towel. Pull the skin toward you while the knife moves in small sawing strokes the other way, so the knife barely travels.

why.title: Portion by weight
why.body: The front of a side is thick and the tail is thin. Cutting by weight, about 150 grams each, with wider pieces at the tail and narrower at the head, gives portions that cook in the same time.

why.title: Reduce the glaze first
why.body: Soy, mirin, and honey cooked down in a saucepan until syrupy cling to the fish. Brushed on thin, they burn before reducing; reduced first, they only need to set in the oven.

why.title: Fish at 145°F
why.body: The app's standard for fish is 145°F in the thickest part. Salmon at 145°F is opaque and flakes; pull it as soon as it gets there.

wrong.sign: The knife cut through the skin
wrong.fix: The blade angled down. Keep it flat against the board and let the pull of the skin do the work.

wrong.sign: Bits of flesh left on the skin
wrong.fix: That's normal at first. Scrape them off with a spoon and add them to a portion before roasting.

wrong.sign: The glaze burned on the pan
wrong.fix: It was brushed on too early or too thick. Brush only once, for the last few minutes.
They were too thin. Fold the tail under itself next time to make it as thick as the rest.

quiz.q: Which way do you pull pin bones?
choices: Toward the head end, at the angle they lie

quiz.q: Why portion by weight instead of by width?
choices: The side's thickness changes, so equal weights cook more evenly

quiz.q: What temperature is salmon done at in this app?

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle, and line the sheet pan with parchment.
Rinse the rice until the water runs nearly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water in the medium saucepan, cover, and cook on low. Rest it off the heat, covered.
Grate the ginger and garlic into the light saucepan with the soy sauce, mirin, and honey. Simmer until syrupy and reduced by about half.
Lay the side skin down on the board. Feel along the thick half and pull each pin bone with the tweezers, toward the head end.
Skin the side from the tail end, holding the skin with a paper towel and keeping the blade flat. Throw the skin away.
Cut the side into 6 portions of about 150 grams, weighing each, wider at the tail. Fold any thin tail piece under. Season with the salt and lay them on the pan.
steps.look: Six portions within about 15 grams of each other.

steps.text: Wash your hands, the knife, the tweezers, and the board with hot, soapy water.
Roast the salmon, then brush the tops with half the glaze and roast until set.
Check the thickest portion from the side: at least 145°F.
Slice the green onions. Serve each portion over rice with a spoonful of the remaining glaze, the green onions, and sesame seeds.
